subject: Predict values of a latent variable correctly

messages.author: c7ea9889adb627cb
messages.subject: Predict values of a latent variable correctly
parts:
Hello all together,

I want to predict the values of a latent variable ("PUW") in a multilevel sem. Therefore, I used two different methods which resulted in very different values. That is why I wanted you to ask, which approach is the right one.

Approach 1 (insert level-2 into the predict-command):
model1<- 'P =~ in1
I =~ im + imo
BEW=~ bm + bmo
HaA=~ hm + hmo
D=~BEW+HaA
PUW =~ P + I + D'

model_1 <- sem(Wunsch, data = dat, meanstructure=TRUE, missing = "FIML", estimator = "MLR", std.lv = TRUE, fixed.x=FALSE)

lavPredict(model_1, level = ko)

Approach 2 (insert level-2 into the model-definitions):
model1 <- "level: 1
P =~ in1
I =~ im + imo
BEW=~ bm + bmo
HaA=~ hm + hmo
D=~BEW+HaA
PUW =~ P + I + D
level: 2
in1 ~~ im + imo + bm+ bmo + hm + hmo
im ~~ imo + bm+ bmo + hm + hmo
imo ~~ bm+ bmo + hm + hmo
bm ~~ bmo + hm + hmo
bmo ~~ hm + hmo
hm ~~ hmo"

model_1 <- sem(model3, data = DatenpuwneufuerMITest, meanstructure=TRUE, cluster = "ko", missing = "FIML", estimator = "MLR", std.lv = TRUE, fixed.x=FALSE)

lavPredict(model_1)

Many thanks in advance!
Best regards,
Robin

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Predict values of a latent variable correctly
parts: which approach is the right one

As the help page says, the level= argument is "Only used in a multilevel SEM", so it is ignored when you use lavPredict() on a single-level model that ignores clustering.
